Safety, respect, honesty, professionalism and accountability are the standard for every TRYP Driver.

This Code applies whenever a Driver is online, accepting requests, travelling to a Passenger, transporting a Passenger, completing a Trip, communicating through TRYP, handling Passenger property or using Passenger information obtained through TRYP.

1. Purpose

The TRYP Driver Code of Conduct ("Code") establishes the standards expected from every Driver using the TRYP platform. It protects Passengers and Drivers, promotes road safety, maintains professional standards, prevents harassment, discrimination and fraud, protects personal information and provides a fair framework for handling violations. It applies while a Driver is online, accepting or completing Trips, communicating through TRYP, handling Passenger property or using Passenger information. Confidentiality and data obligations continue after a Driver stops using TRYP.

2. Our core principles

Every Driver is expected to follow five principles: Safety — get the Passenger there safely; Respect — treat people with dignity; Honesty — do not manipulate Trips, fares, ratings, Documents, Accounts or payments; Professionalism — represent TRYP responsibly; and Accountability — take responsibility and cooperate with legitimate investigations.

3. The golden rule

Never deliberately do something to a Passenger that you would reasonably object to happening to yourself or your family. This includes threatening, intimidating, following, harassing, touching without consent, stealing, manipulating fares, exposing private information or driving dangerously.

4. Safety comes first

Always prioritise safety over Earnings, Trip completion, ratings, Passenger demands, time targets, bonuses or acceptance rates. A Driver may refuse or terminate a Trip where continuing creates a genuine safety risk, provided the Driver acts reasonably and lawfully.

5. Professional Driver behaviour

Be reasonably polite, communicate clearly, avoid unnecessary arguments, respect privacy, drive responsibly, keep the Vehicle clean, follow lawful instructions and use reasonable judgement. Do not deliberately create an intimidating environment.

6. Zero-tolerance conduct

Physical or sexual assault, kidnapping, unlawful confinement, robbery, serious threats, dangerous or impaired driving, deliberate fraud, identity theft, serious privacy violations, GPS manipulation, account selling or renting, and deliberate Platform hacking are serious violations. They may result in immediate suspension and permanent removal.

7. Driver identity

The Driver must always be the person registered to the Driver Account. Friends, family, employees, other Drivers and unregistered persons may not operate under the Account.

8. No Account renting

Do not rent, sell or lease a TRYP Account, including arrangements such as “use my Driver Account while I am away”. Account sharing is prohibited.

9. Driver verification

Complete required identity verification personally. Do not use another identity, submit false, modified or expired Documents, defeat facial verification or use another person’s photograph.

10. Vehicle identity

The Vehicle used for Trips must match the Vehicle registered on the Driver Account. Do not secretly substitute another Vehicle. Passengers must be able to verify Driver and Vehicle information shown by the Platform.

11. Operating licence

Maintain every licence or permit required by law. Do not provide the affected service when a required operating licence is invalid. TRYP may deactivate the Driver or Vehicle until valid documentation is supplied. The amended South African e-hailing framework commenced on 12 September 2025 and is available through the South African Government ↗.

Reference: South African Government e-hailing framework ↗

12. Vehicle roadworthiness

Never knowingly operate a dangerous or unroadworthy Vehicle. Before going online, reasonably check tyres, brakes, lights, indicators, seatbelts, doors, mirrors, windscreen, fuel and general mechanical condition.

13. Vehicle cleanliness

Keep the Passenger area reasonably clean and suitable for transportation. Remove excessive rubbish, food waste, strong odours, dangerous objects and excessive clutter.

14. Smoking

Do not smoke in a manner prohibited by law or TRYP policy. Avoid leaving the Vehicle with an excessive smoke odour.

15. Alcohol and drugs

Never drive for TRYP while impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, misused medication or another substance. If you are not fit to drive, go offline.

16. Fatigue

Do not continue driving when too tired to drive safely. No bonus or Trip target overrides the responsibility to rest and drive safely.

17. Speed

Obey applicable speed limits and road and weather conditions. Aggressive driving to complete more Trips is prohibited.

18. Reckless driving

Do not race, tailgate, weave aggressively, drive unlawfully on pavements, ignore signals, perform dangerous manoeuvres or intentionally intimidate road users.

19. Mobile phones

Comply with South African laws concerning mobile-phone use while driving. Configure the Driver App before driving and do not interact with the phone in a way that creates a hazard.

20. Navigation

Use navigation responsibly. You remain responsible for safe driving even when navigation is wrong. A reasonable alternative route may be used for traffic, closures, safety, construction, weather, Passenger request or navigation error.

21. Route manipulation

Never take unnecessarily long routes solely to increase a Fare. Do not drive in circles, pass the destination and return, take unnecessary detours or keep a Trip active after arrival.

22. GPS spoofing

Do not use fake GPS applications, location spoofing, emulator manipulation, device-based manipulation or software designed to falsify Driver location.

23. Fake Trips

Do not self-book, ask friends to create fake Trips, create Trips without carrying a Passenger, end fake Trips or artificially generate kilometres.

24. Trip manipulation

Do not manipulate pickup, destination, duration, distance, status, Fare or cancellation information.

25. Accepting Trips

Accept or decline Trips using available TRYP functionality. Once accepted, make reasonable efforts to complete the Trip unless a legitimate reason prevents completion.

26. Cancellations

Cancel only where reasonably necessary, including an unlocatable Passenger, unsafe pickup, Vehicle problem, emergency, Passenger behaviour, unlawful request, capacity issue or genuine safety concern.

27. Abusive cancellation

Do not cancel for unlawful discriminatory reasons or manipulate cancellation systems to avoid areas, increase incentives, avoid specific Passengers or alter statistics.

28. Passenger pickup

Park safely, avoid dangerous locations, reasonably confirm the Passenger, ensure Vehicle details match the App and allow safe entry.

29. Passenger verification

Reasonably verify that the person entering is associated with the Trip. Do not demand excessive personal information.

30. Passenger privacy

Passenger information may include name, photograph, phone number, pickup, destination, Trip history and payment information. Use it only for legitimate TRYP purposes.

31. No stalking

Never follow a Passenger, visit their home after a Trip, wait outside their workplace, track movements or repeatedly contact them.

32. No personal solicitation

Do not build a private customer list or pressure Passengers for personal numbers, social-media accounts, email addresses or home information.

33. Off-platform solicitation

Do not move TRYP Passengers off-platform for personal gain. “Cancel and I will take you privately”, “save my number” and “I will give you a cheaper price” are prohibited.

34. Fares

Accept the Fare calculated or displayed by the applicable TRYP system. Do not invent additional charges.

35. Cash

Where cash is supported, collect only the applicable amount, provide reasonable change where possible, record the Trip correctly and report payment problems honestly.

36. No double charging

Never knowingly collect both the full cash Fare and the same Fare electronically. Follow the payment-dispute process when a problem occurs.

37. Tolls

Handle tolls according to TRYP fare rules. Never invent toll charges.

38. Payment fraud

Do not claim payment was not received, create fake payment records, manipulate cash Trips, collude, use stolen payment information or create artificial transactions.

39. Ratings

Do not pressure Passengers for positive ratings, threaten them over ratings or offer money or benefits for ratings.

40. Rating retaliation

A low rating is not permission to threaten, contact, follow, harass or falsely report a Passenger.

41. Discrimination

Do not unlawfully discriminate or refuse service because of protected characteristics. Treat every Passenger fairly.

42. Respectful communication

Do not use racial slurs, sexual insults, threats, hate speech, degrading language or intimidation.

43. Sexual conduct

Zero tolerance applies to unwanted sexual comments, intrusive questions, propositions, sexual touching, exposure, requests for sexual acts, sexual messages, sexual photographs or sexual use of Passenger information.

44. Physical contact

Avoid unnecessary physical contact. Sexual, threatening or aggressive contact is prohibited.

45. Threats

Never threaten violence, property damage, exposure of private information, false reporting or physical retaliation.

46. Conflicts with Passengers

Remain calm, avoid escalation, stop somewhere safe if necessary, contact support and end the Trip safely if continuation is unreasonable. Never turn an ordinary disagreement into a physical confrontation.

47. Passenger intoxication

Intoxication is not automatically a reason for refusal. Refuse or end a Trip only where the Passenger creates a genuine safety risk and law and TRYP policy permit it.

48. Passenger aggression

If a Passenger becomes violent or presents an immediate threat, move to safety, end the Trip safely, use emergency functionality and contact emergency services where necessary.

49. Weapons

Comply with applicable weapons law. Do not facilitate unlawful transportation and do not physically confront a suspected Passenger beyond what is necessary for immediate safety.

50. Illegal goods

Do not knowingly transport illegal goods. Where suspicious circumstances create a serious safety concern, prioritise safety and contact appropriate authorities where appropriate.

51. Service animals

Comply with legal requirements for recognised service animals. Do not falsely classify a legitimate service animal as an ordinary pet to avoid carrying it.

52. Pets

Apply reasonable TRYP rules for ordinary pets and ride categories. Refusal must not be used to discriminate against a service animal.

53. Children

Comply with laws concerning children. Do not knowingly transport children unlawfully or unsafely, and do not exploit or solicit children.

54. Child safety

Never make sexual comments to children, photograph them for personal reasons, contact them outside legitimate Trip purposes, offer unrelated services or establish inappropriate relationships.

55. Lost property

Report property left in the Vehicle through TRYP. Do not keep, sell, use, destroy, hide it or demand unreasonable payment for return.

56. Returning property

Cooperate reasonably with the lost-property process and reasonable arrangements for return.

57. Accidents

Prioritise safety, stop safely, check injuries, contact emergency services, provide reasonable assistance, notify TRYP and cooperate with investigations.

58. Emergencies

Use available safety tools when necessary. If TRYP provides an emergency or panic feature, use it responsibly. The South African framework also addresses panic-button safety measures in e-hailing vehicles. See the future Safety & Emergency Response Policy for the operational escalation process.

59. False emergency reports

Do not deliberately abuse emergency functionality. Good-faith use is protected even if the event later proves not to require emergency intervention.

60. Dashcam and recording

Comply with privacy and data-protection law when using cameras. Do not post, sell, unnecessarily share or use recordings to harass Passengers.

61. Social media

Never publish Passenger images, videos, names, addresses, destinations, phone numbers or personal information without lawful authority or permission.

62. Confidentiality

Keep information obtained through TRYP confidential. This obligation survives termination of the Driver Account.

63. POPIA

Handle Passenger information responsibly. POPIA governs lawful processing and protection of personal information. Review the Information Regulator guidance ↗, the Information Regulator eServices portal ↗ and the final Driver Privacy Notice.

Reference: Information Regulator ↗

64. Driver data

TRYP may process Driver information for identity verification, payments, safety, compliance, fraud prevention, platform operation and regulatory requirements. The applicable Privacy Policy explains processing.

65. Cybersecurity

Do not hack TRYP, steal credentials, abuse APIs, introduce malware, scrape without authority, reverse engineer for malicious purposes or bypass security controls.

66. Bots

Do not use automation to accept or reject Trips, manipulate incentives or demand, or generate fake activity.

67. Multiple Accounts

Do not create multiple identities to evade suspension, manipulate incentives, circumvent verification, manipulate ratings or generate fraud.

68. Collusion

Do not coordinate with Passengers or Drivers to create fake Trips, ratings, referrals, cancellations, artificial demand or fraudulent promotions.

69. Referral fraud

Use referral programs honestly. Do not refer yourself or create fake Passenger or Driver Accounts.

70. Promotion abuse

Promotions reward legitimate activity, not artificial activity. Do not manipulate bonuses or incentives.

71. Driver-Passenger relationships

Respect the professional boundary. Never pressure a Passenger into dating, friendship, sexual activity, personal meetings or unrelated business.

72. Passenger consent

Using TRYP does not consent to touching, sexual comments, personal photography, personal recording, contact, dating or sexual activity.

73. No retaliation

Do not retaliate against a Passenger who complains, reports misconduct, gives a low rating, refuses personal contact, requests another route or uses safety functionality.

74. Driver responsibility for Vehicle

Keep fuel, tyres, brakes, lights, seatbelts, roadworthiness and Documents ready for every Trip.

75. Vehicle modifications

Do not make modifications that make the Vehicle unsafe or non-compliant.

76. Passenger seatbelts

Give Passengers the opportunity to use available seatbelts and comply with road-traffic laws.

77. Overloading

Never carry more Passengers than the legally permitted capacity.

78. Boot/loading area

Never transport a Passenger in a boot, luggage compartment or area not legally designed for Passengers.

79. Dangerous items in Vehicle

Do not keep dangerous objects where they could injure Passengers.

80. Vehicle security

Take reasonable steps to secure the Vehicle, Passenger belongings, Driver device and TRYP information.

81. Cash security

Take reasonable precautions when carrying cash and do not expose unnecessary amounts.

82. Unsafe pickup locations

Decline or modify pickup when stopping creates a genuine safety or legal problem, such as active lanes, dangerous intersections, prohibited stopping or immediate crime threats.

83. Unsafe destinations

If a destination creates an immediate safety concern, contact support or use safety procedures rather than escalating directly with the Passenger.

84. Route privacy

Do not reveal or exploit information about a Passenger’s destination.

85. Personal information after the Trip

Once the Trip ends, do not retain or use Passenger information for unrelated purposes.

86. Passenger contact after Trip

Contact after a Trip is limited to legitimate reasons such as lost property, a Trip dispute, a safety matter or TRYP-authorised communication.

87. Driver-Passenger communication

Use TRYP communications responsibly. Messages must not contain threats, sexual content, hate speech, unwanted solicitation, harassment or fraudulent requests.

88. Recording communications

Comply with applicable laws when recording calls or communications.

89. Law enforcement requests

Comply with lawful requests from authorised authorities. TRYP may cooperate with lawful investigations.

90. Criminal conduct

Nothing prevents TRYP from reporting suspected criminal conduct where appropriate or legally required.

91. Driver complaints

Drivers may report Passenger misconduct, safety concerns, fraud, payment problems, Vehicle problems, harassment and Platform problems. Genuine good-faith complaints are protected.

92. Passenger complaints

Passengers may report Driver misconduct. A complaint does not automatically mean guilt; TRYP may assess evidence.

93. Fair investigation

Where reasonably possible, TRYP may receive a complaint, assess seriousness, apply safety measures, review evidence, request information, invite a response and decide.

94. Temporary suspension

A Driver may be suspended during a serious investigation. Suspension is a safety or investigative measure and does not necessarily prove the allegation.

95. Driver appeal

Where available, provide an explanation, Trip information, evidence and witness information through the appeal process.

96. Evidence TRYP may consider

TRYP may consider GPS, Trip and App records, payments, communications, reports, ratings, photographs, videos, Vehicle information and device/security information lawfully obtained.

97. Evidence is not automatic guilt

Distinguish between an allegation, evidence and a finding. A complaint should not automatically be treated as proof.

98. Severity levels

TRYP may classify violations as Level 1 Minor, Level 2 Moderate, Level 3 Serious or Level 4 Critical. Classification considers safety, integrity, intent, evidence and history.
Level 1 · MinorWarning, education or reminder.
Level 2 · ModerateTraining, restriction or account review.
Level 3 · SeriousImmediate suspension, investigation or removal.
Level 4 · CriticalImmediate suspension and possible permanent termination.

99. Examples of Level 1 violations

Poor cleanliness, minor communication problems, non-critical procedure failures or failure to update non-critical information may result in a warning, education, reminder or temporary restriction.

100. Examples of Level 2 violations

Repeated cancellation abuse, fare disputes, repeated poor conduct, unauthorised solicitation, repeated Vehicle-standard failures or rating manipulation may result in warnings, training, suspension, adjustments or review.

101. Examples of Level 3 violations

Fraud, GPS manipulation, fake Trips, Account sharing, serious harassment, deliberate Fare manipulation, repeated safety violations or Passenger-data misuse may result in immediate suspension, investigation, removal or referral.

102. Examples of Level 4 violations

Sexual assault, serious physical assault, kidnapping, serious threats, robbery, dangerous driving causing serious harm, deliberate identity fraud, major payment fraud, cyberattack or deliberate Passenger exploitation may result in immediate suspension and permanent termination.

103. Consequences are not automatic

TRYP may consider severity, evidence, history, intent, safety, frequency and whether conduct was deliberate. A different response may apply where circumstances justify it.

104. Repeat offenders

Repeated violations may result in progressively stronger action. Repeated minor violations may eventually lead to suspension or termination.

105. Serious violations may skip warnings

TRYP does not need to issue three warnings before acting. A critical safety violation may justify immediate action.

106. Good-faith errors

Not every mistake is misconduct. TRYP may distinguish honest mistakes, negligence, recklessness, deliberate misconduct and fraud.

107. Cooperation

Cooperate reasonably with legitimate investigations by providing Trip information, explanations, Documents, Vehicle information and relevant evidence.

108. False information during investigations

Knowingly providing false information to investigators may constitute a separate violation.

109. Deleting evidence

Do not deliberately destroy or manipulate relevant evidence after learning of a legitimate investigation.

110. Privacy during investigations

TRYP should limit investigation access to information reasonably necessary for the matter, subject to legal and safety requirements.

111. Protection against retaliation

TRYP prohibits retaliation against Passengers, Drivers, employees, contractors or other people making genuine reports or participating in investigations.

112. False reporting

Deliberately fabricated complaints may constitute misconduct. Honest complaints that are not proven are not automatically false.

113. Driver safety

Drivers may also be victims of robbery, assault, harassment, fraud and violence. Report incidents through TRYP safety systems.

114. Passenger safety

Drivers contribute to a safe environment but are not security officers, police or medical professionals. Act reasonably and safely during emergencies.

115. No vigilante action

Do not take unnecessary physical action against Passengers or suspected criminals. Contact emergency services or law enforcement where appropriate.

116. Emergency location

Where supported, TRYP safety systems may use available Trip/location information to assist an incident response.

117. Driver training

TRYP may require training on safety, Platform use, conduct, anti-discrimination, privacy, fraud, emergency procedures and Vehicle standards.

118. Training compliance

Training may be required before activating a category, returning from suspension, continuing a service or meeting new regulatory requirements.

119. Accessibility

Reasonably accommodate Passengers with disabilities in accordance with law and TRYP policy. Do not use disability as an excuse for discrimination.

120. Professional appearance

Maintain a clean and professional appearance suitable for Passenger transportation.

121. Uniform

If TRYP introduces an official uniform, comply with applicable uniform requirements.

122. TRYP brand

Do not use TRYP branding to imply personal ownership, employment where none exists, official government status or authority beyond your actual role.

123. Unauthorised advertising

Do not place unauthorised advertising, stickers or commercial material on or inside the Vehicle in a way that misrepresents TRYP, harms safety, violates law or interferes with identification.

124. Driver feedback

Provide constructive feedback about App functionality, safety, Passenger conduct, Vehicle standards, payments and support.

125. Platform abuse

Do not overload support with false complaints, duplicate requests, threats, abusive messages or fraudulent claims.

126. Support staff

Treat TRYP support staff respectfully. Abuse or threats toward support staff may result in action.

127. No bribery

Do not offer or request bribes involving TRYP employees, support, Drivers, Passengers, inspectors or authorities.

128. Conflict of interest

Disclose relevant conflicts where TRYP reasonably requires disclosure.

129. Outside business

Lawful outside business is allowed unless restricted, but do not use Passenger information from TRYP to build an unrelated customer base.

130. Driver responsibility

Being a TRYP Driver means accepting responsibility for your conduct, Vehicle, driving, Account, Documents, treatment of Passengers and use of Passenger information.

131. Three simple rules

RULE 1: DRIVE SAFELY.RULE 2: TREAT PEOPLE WITH RESPECT.RULE 3: DON’T CHEAT THE PLATFORM OR THE PASSENGER.

132. Serious breach

Access may be suspended or terminated for conduct materially threatening Passenger, Driver or public safety, TRYP security or financial integrity, regulatory compliance or privacy.

133. Relationship with Driver Terms

This Code forms part of the TRYP Driver Terms & Conditions and should be read with the TRYP Driver Agreement. If there is a conflict, applicable law and mandatory regulation take priority, then the Driver Agreement, Driver Terms, then this Code as an operational standard.

134. Changes to this Code

TRYP may update the Code to improve safety, address fraud, comply with law, improve service or address emerging risks. Material changes may be communicated through the Driver App or another appropriate channel.

135. Driver acknowledgement

By activating Driver Mode, accepting Trips or continuing to use TRYP, the Driver confirms they have read and understand this Code, agree to follow it, understand possible warnings, restrictions, suspension or termination, and understand that serious misconduct may result in immediate action.

TRYP should also maintain a separate Safety & Emergency Response Policy covering SOS, accidents, robbery, assault, medical emergencies, evidence preservation, law-enforcement requests and post-incident support.
